edges.description: Infection is the first step of the Correa cascade that constitutes this node's carcinogenic substrate.

A review-level risk-factor listing names smoking alongside H. pylori and salt intake, but does not itself trace a mechanistic route into the carcinogenic cascade, so the intermediates are unknown rather than known.

Excess salt injures the gastric mucosa, worsening the gastritis/atrophy stages of the carcinogenic cascade that H. pylori infection triggers. Mucosal injury is the known intervening step, and is not itself a node in this graph.

nodes.description: Metastatic gastric cancer arises from a primary gastric adenocarcinoma that develops through the multistep Correa cascade of chronic gastritis, atrophy, intestinal metaplasia, and dysplasia. This upstream carcinogenic process, not modeled elsewhere in this entry, precedes the invasive and metastatic biology modeled by the other nodes in this entry.

evidence.reference_title: Human gastric carcinogenesis: a multistep and multifactorial process--First American Cancer Society Award Lecture on Cancer Epidemiology and Prevention.
evidence.snippet: Evidence from pathology and epidemiology studies has been provided for a human model of gastric carcinogenesis with the following sequential stages: chronic gastritis; atrophy; intestinal metaplasia; and dysplasia.

evidence.reference_title: [Advances in the application of intragastric flora in the diagnosis and treatment of gastric cancer].
evidence.snippet: Gastric cancer is one of the major causes of cancer-related deaths worldwide, and infection with Helicobacter pylori and EBV, smoking and a salt-heavy diet have been shown to be risk factors for the development of gastric cancer.
